summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol and opioid dependence, alcoholic cirrhosis, and asthma was admitted for severe epigastric, right upper quadrant, and left upper quadrant abdominal pain following a relapse involving a pint of hard alcohol. The pain, radiating to the back and worsened by meals, was consistent with acute alcoholic hepatitis and chronic pancreatitis flare. He was managed supportively with IV fluids, bowel rest, and pain control, and monitored for alcohol withdrawal using CIWA without complications. Imaging showed a diffusely echogenic liver, reversal of portal vein flow, and pericholecystic fluid without gallstones. Liver enzymes and symptoms improved during the hospitalization. He expressed motivation to remain abstinent, and plans were made to restart Suboxone and arrange follow-up with hepatology and addiction services. He was discharged home with a short-term oxycodone prescription, lorazepam for anxiety, and continuation of all chronic medications.
